To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthetic N-acetyl-D-hexosamine-based tetrasaccharides 49 and 52 are the best endogenous ligands for CD69 so far, that the tetrasacchride 68 is the first synthetic ligand for CD 69 that can activate the receptor, and that this compound is the best candidate for the development of a novel carbohydrate-based immunomodu-lator.
a tetrasaccharidic ligand of CD69 was designed, and its dimerization by a hydrophilic linker resulted in a compound that activated CD69(+) killer lymphocytes and enhanced natural killing in vitro.
a fully branched synthetic tetrasaccharides, a mimetic for the endogenous ligands for CD69, was found to activate CD69+ killer cells via dimerization via the hydrophilic flexible linkage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new class of carbohydrate-based immunomimetic drugs.
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of carbohydrate-based mimics for CD69, an endogenous ligands for CD69.
the synthesis of branched and linear N-acetyl-d-glucosamine homooligosaccharides and their evaluation as ligands for the CD69 leukocyte activation antigen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD69 is a carbohydrate-binding receptor that recognizes the GlcNAcb1-4GlcNAc sequence in a branched oligosaccharidic context.
the endogenous ligands for the leukocyte receptor CD69 are branched oligosaccharides of a defined structure, which can be mimicked by synthetic oligosaccharidic ligands.

the CD69 receptor is a promising target for carbohydrate-based immunotherapy, and that a fully synthetic branched tetrasacharide mimetic of the CD69 ligand, dimerized via a hydrophillic flexible linker, is an effective activator of the receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a fully branched tetra- or hexasaccharide mimetic of the natural ligand for CD 69 can be prepared synthetically, and that such a compound can activate killer lymphocytes in vitro.
the tetrasacchride 52, which is a mimetic of an endogenous ligands for CD69, has a potential to be a lead compound for a novel antitumor drug.
the endogenous CD69 ligand has been identified as a branched N-acetyld-hexosamine oligosaccharides, and a mimetic has been designed and synthesized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fully branched tetrameric N-acetyl-d-glucosamine oligosaccharides, mimicking the endogenous CD69 ligand, can be used as a ligand for CD 69.

the CD69 receptor, which was thought to recognize only linear oligosaccharides, is capable of recognizing branched structures, and even tetrasaccharides, as well as their dimerized forms, with high affinity.
the CD69(2) homodimer is the functional unit of CD69 and that the tetrasacchride GlcNAcb(3)GlcNAcb(4)GlcNAca(6)GlcNac is the minimal structure required for the activation of CD69.
